CipherBox v1 has **no production deployment** (as of 2026-07-19) — only the staging environment exists, and both desktop and web authenticate against Web3Auth **DEVNET** (free tier). MAINNET has never been used by any real identity. Production release (web or desktop) is deliberately deferred until billing revenue or investment funds Web3Auth MAINNET authentication.

**Why:** Code configs are misleading here — web maps `production → MAINNET` (`apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/core-kit.ts:6-11`) while desktop maps all envs including production to DEVNET (`apps/desktop/src/auth.ts:54-59`). This "keypair split" is latent, never-exercised prod config, not an operational issue.

**How to apply:** Don't treat production Web3Auth config paths as live or flag the desktop/web network divergence as an active bug — it's unshipped config. v2 decided a clean break on data and no identity-continuity obligation (see [[cipher-box-next-wayfinder-map]], ticket "Decide: v1 vault migration stance").
--- project-web-e2e-only-on-main-push
name: project-web-e2e-only-on-main-push
description: Web E2E does not run on PRs — only on push to main (and manual dispatch); how a regression slipped through
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa272e9e-42b1-4669-b018-72e17add5018
  modified: 2026-08-08T17:59:20.846Z

**OBSOLETE for v2 as of 2026-08-08 — the title claim no longer holds.** `ci.yml` triggers on
`pull_request: branches: [main]` and calls `web-e2e.yml` as a `workflow_call` at `ci.yml:890`, gated
on the `web` or `e2e` path filters (`ci.yml:72-76`) and behind a stable always-reporting result gate
that branch protection requires. So **Web E2E Smoke DOES run on a v2 PR** when the PR touches a path
it covers. `web-e2e.yml` itself is now `workflow_dispatch` + `workflow_call` only — it has no `push`
trigger at all. The rest of this memory is v1 history: the flake and local-confirmation techniques
below still read true, the trigger claim does not.

The `ci-e2e.yml` "CI E2E Tests" workflow triggers only on `push: branches: [main]` and `workflow_dispatch`. On PRs the "Web E2E" job does NOT run — PRs show only `SDK E2E Tests` + a `Verify E2E Passed` gate (which passes when web-e2e is skipped). So a web regression is first observed on the **post-merge push to main**, not on the PR.

**Why it matters:** PR #494 (phase 47 SDK folder-state/publish consolidation) broke `writable-shares.spec.ts:330` ("4.3 Alice edits Bob's file") and it passed all PR checks, then failed Web E2E on the main push. Confirm regressions by comparing the failing commit to its parent's Web E2E run (`gh run list --workflow ci-e2e.yml --branch main`).

**How to verify a web fix before merge:** push the branch and manually dispatch. Two options:

- **Web-only (faster, preferred):** `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh workflow run web-e2e.yml --ref <branch>` — `web-e2e.yml` is directly `workflow_dispatch`-enabled and checks out `ref: inputs.ref || github.sha` = the branch HEAD, so it runs the identical Web E2E job against branch code with no merge. Direct dispatch resolves repo secrets directly (no `secrets: inherit` parent needed), so it faithfully reproduces the main-push run.
- **Both web+desktop:** `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh workflow run ci-e2e.yml --ref <branch>` (dispatch forces both via the `Force all changes on manual dispatch` step). Poll the "Web E2E" job specifically.

This was the gap behind the **#498** regression (self-bootstrap folderTree clobber) too — tracked/fixed as Phase 48 REQ-1, whose acceptance gate is a pre-merge `web-e2e.yml` dispatch.

**Single-worker cascade-abort HIDES regressions (PR #555, 2026-06-24).** `playwright.config.ts` is `workers:1, fullyParallel:false, retries:0` and CI caps max-failures, so tests run sequentially in alphabetical file order and the run ABORTS after a couple failures — every later test shows "did not run". A flaky EARLY test (`invite-link-workflow` 1.1 account-creation, `journey-timing` login-to-vault, `media-preview` upload — all chronically flaky) skips the whole tail. `writable-shares` sorts LAST, so across 3 dispatches a real regression in it was repeatedly masked (the run never reached it; its discard-warning signature was absent only because the path wasn't exercised). Lesson: a web-e2e dispatch that fails on a *different* early test each run does NOT clear your test — don't infer pass from absence-in-failures. Captured as todo `.planning/todos/pending/2026-06-24-web-e2e-flaky-cascade-abort.md`.

**Confirm a single spec LOCALLY when CI flakes can't reach it.** Playwright's `webServer` block auto-starts mock-ipns + API (`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api dev`) + web (`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web dev`) with `reuseExistingServer: !CI`, and `.env` files already exist locally. With the stack up (postgres 5432, kubo 5001, redis 6380, mock 3001) just run `cd tests/web-e2e && pnpm exec playwright test writable-shares.spec.ts --project=chromium` — the `describe.serial` block is self-contained (creates its own Alice/Bob accounts) and runs in ~1.5 min, in isolation, no flaky early tests to abort it. This directly confirmed the #555 fix (29/29) when CI couldn't.

Related: [[project-web-sdk-folder-state-desync]], [[project-web-vitest-include-test-only]], [[project-ipns-resolve-ed25519-pubkey-from-name]].

=== v1 Dockerfile
# CipherBox API - Multi-stage Docker build
# Build from repo root: docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile -t cipherbox-api .

# Stage 1: Install dependencies and build TypeScript
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate
WORKDIR /app
COPY pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml package.json ./
COPY apps/api/package.json apps/api/
COPY packages/crypto/package.json packages/crypto/
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter @cipherbox/api...
COPY apps/api/ apps/api/
COPY packages/crypto/ packages/crypto/
COPY tsconfig.base.json ./
RUN pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build && pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build

# Create standalone deployment (flat node_modules, no symlinks)
RUN pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api deploy /deploy --prod --legacy

# Stage 2: Production runtime
FROM node:22-alpine AS production
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S appgroup && adduser -S appuser -u 1001 -G appgroup
WORKDIR /app

COPY --from=build /deploy/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/apps/api/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /deploy/package.json ./package.json

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV PORT=3000

USER appuser
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]

=== v1 run-migrations
/**
 * Programmatic migration runner for Docker containers.
 *
 * The TypeORM CLI (via ts-node) is not available in production images.
 * This script runs migrations using compiled JS entities and migrations.
 *
 * Usage (inside Docker container):
 *   node dist/run-migrations.js
 */
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';
import { config } from 'dotenv';

config();

const dataSource = new DataSource({
  type: 'postgres',
  host: process.env.DB_HOST || 'localhost',
  port: parseInt(process.env.DB_PORT || '5432', 10),
  username: process.env.DB_USERNAME || 'postgres',
  password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD || 'postgres',
  database: process.env.DB_DATABASE || 'cipherbox',
  entities: ['dist/**/*.entity.js'],
  migrations: ['dist/migrations/*.js'],
  logging: ['error', 'migration'],
});

async function run() {
  try {
    await dataSource.initialize();
    console.log('Running migrations...');
    const migrations = await dataSource.runMigrations();
    if (migrations.length === 0) {
      console.log('No pending migrations.');
    } else {
      console.log(`Applied ${migrations.length} migration(s):`);
      for (const m of migrations) {
        console.log(`  - ${m.name}`);
      }
    }
    await dataSource.destroy();
    console.log('Migrations complete.');
    process.exit(0);
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    const err = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));
    console.error(
      'Migration failed:',
      err.name || 'UnknownError',
      err.message?.replace(/((?:host|password|user(?:name)?)=)[^\s;,]+/gi, '$1***') || ''
    );
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

run();

# Stock Caddy ships no rate limiter, and the front's `/routing/v1` PUT publish
# leg is deliberately token-free (blueprint/api.md, Egress) — a body cap is all
# it can bound without one.
#
# Both stages are digest-pinned: this binary terminates TLS and enforces every
# egress obligation, and the same tags feed the Lint gate. The builder bakes the
# Caddy version, so `xcaddy build` takes it from there rather than repeating it
# here, where a bump could miss one of two places and mismatch the runtime base.
FROM caddy:2.11.4-builder-alpine@sha256:7bac9be4072f7c4db2ccc7350750e0705004bf02da2ac7d96b1469ca4f28bb7c AS build

# Pinned to a commit rather than v0.1.0, the newest tag: `ipv6_prefix` landed
# after it, and masking the key to a /64 outside the module means pattern-matching
# a text address, which cannot reach the network half of a compressed one.
RUN xcaddy build --with github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit@5625512f24f6f59d6f64fb3aafe5eecff0b286db

FROM caddy:2.11.4-alpine@sha256:5f5c8640aae01df9654968d946d8f1a56c497f1dd5c5cda4cf95ab7c14d58648

COPY --from=build /usr/bin/caddy /usr/bin/caddy

=== v1 Dockerfile
# CipherBox API - Multi-stage Docker build
# Build from repo root: docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile -t cipherbox-api .

# Stage 1: Install dependencies and build TypeScript
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate
WORKDIR /app
COPY pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml package.json ./
COPY apps/api/package.json apps/api/
COPY packages/crypto/package.json packages/crypto/
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter @cipherbox/api...
COPY apps/api/ apps/api/
COPY packages/crypto/ packages/crypto/
COPY tsconfig.base.json ./
RUN pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build && pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build

# Create standalone deployment (flat node_modules, no symlinks)
RUN pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api deploy /deploy --prod --legacy

# Stage 2: Production runtime
FROM node:22-alpine AS production
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S appgroup && adduser -S appuser -u 1001 -G appgroup
WORKDIR /app

COPY --from=build /deploy/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/apps/api/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /deploy/package.json ./package.json

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV PORT=3000

USER appuser
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]

/**
 * Programmatic migration runner for Docker containers.
 *
 * The TypeORM CLI (via ts-node) is not available in production images.
 * This script runs migrations using compiled JS entities and migrations.
 *
 * Usage (inside Docker container):
 *   node dist/run-migrations.js
 */
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';
import { config } from 'dotenv';

config();

const dataSource = new DataSource({
  type: 'postgres',
  host: process.env.DB_HOST || 'localhost',
  port: parseInt(process.env.DB_PORT || '5432', 10),
  username: process.env.DB_USERNAME || 'postgres',
  password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD || 'postgres',
  database: process.env.DB_DATABASE || 'cipherbox',
  entities: ['dist/**/*.entity.js'],
  migrations: ['dist/migrations/*.js'],
  logging: ['error', 'migration'],
});

async function run() {
  try {
    await dataSource.initialize();
    console.log('Running migrations...');
    const migrations = await dataSource.runMigrations();
    if (migrations.length === 0) {
      console.log('No pending migrations.');
    } else {
      console.log(`Applied ${migrations.length} migration(s):`);
      for (const m of migrations) {
        console.log(`  - ${m.name}`);
      }
    }
    await dataSource.destroy();
    console.log('Migrations complete.');
    process.exit(0);
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    const err = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));
    console.error(
      'Migration failed:',
      err.name || 'UnknownError',
      err.message?.replace(/((?:host|password|user(?:name)?)=)[^\s;,]+/gi, '$1***') || ''
    );
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

run();

import { SwaggerModule } from '@nestjs/swagger';
import { buildOpenApiDocument, configureApp, corsOptionsFromEnv } from './app-setup';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

async function bootstrap(): Promise<void> {
  const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' || !process.env.NODE_ENV;

    logger: isDev ? ['log', 'error', 'warn', 'debug', 'verbose'] : ['log', 'error', 'warn'],

  const document = buildOpenApiDocument(app);
  SwaggerModule.setup('api-docs', app, document, { jsonDocumentUrl: 'api-docs/json' });

  const port = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000);
  await app.listen(port);
  logger.log(`CipherBox API listening on http://localhost:${port}`);
}

# The API area of the PR gate (blueprint/testing.md): everything that reads
# `apps/api`. Called by ci.yml. The live contract suite stays in the caller —
# it spans the Rust client and the TypeScript API and belongs to neither area.
name: CI API

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ts:
        description: The TypeScript path filter matched.
        required: true
        type: boolean

permissions: {}

jobs:
  typecheck:
    name: Typecheck (TypeScript)
    if: inputs.ts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0977fd99725f1db4007ccb2928dbb4e90d06cc86 # v6.0.10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run the type checker
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api typecheck

  unit:
    name: Unit tests
    if: inputs.ts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0977fd99725f1db4007ccb2928dbb4e90d06cc86 # v6.0.10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run the API unit suite
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test

  # The first-class API integration suite (blueprint/testing.md law 1): the
  # real-Postgres concurrency and interleaving tests — registry
  # register-vs-retire phantom and duplicate-insert, mailbox pending-cap, and
  # the advisory-lock lock_timeout DoS guard. They are named `*.itest.ts`; this
  # job owns them. Each test provisions its own randomized throwaway database
  # and drops only that one.
  integration:
    name: Integration tests (real Postgres)
    if: inputs.ts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    env:
      DB_HOST: localhost
      DB_PORT: 5432
      DB_USERNAME: postgres
      DB_PASSWORD: postgres
      DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
      NODE_ENV: test
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0977fd99725f1db4007ccb2928dbb4e90d06cc86 # v6.0.10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run the API integration suite
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test:integration

  migration-drift:
    name: Migration drift
    if: inputs.ts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    env:
      DB_HOST: localhost
      DB_PORT: 5432
      DB_USERNAME: postgres
      DB_PASSWORD: postgres
      DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test

changes:
    name: Detect Changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      ts: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.ts }}
      rust: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.rust }}
      web: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.web }}
      e2e: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.e2e }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.desktop }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            ts:
              - 'apps/**'
              - 'packages/**'
              - 'tests/**'
              # The TS suite pins MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES against this manifest, so a
              # Rust-side chunk-size change must run it.
...
  api:
    name: API
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.ts == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci-api.yml
    with:
      ts: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.ts == 'true' }}

  api-result:
    name: API Result
    needs: [changes, api]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Require the API area to pass or be skipped
        env:
          CHANGES_RESULT: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          AREA_RESULT: ${{ needs.api.result }}
        run: |
          echo "changes result: ${CHANGES_RESULT}; api result: ${AREA_RESULT}"
          if [ "${CHANGES_RESULT}" != 'success' ]; then
            echo "::error::change detection ${CHANGES_RESULT}, so the API area never ran"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${AREA_RESULT}" = 'failure' ] || [ "${AREA_RESULT}" = 'cancelled' ]; then
            echo "::error::the API area ${AREA_RESULT}"
            exit 1
          fi

import dataSource from './data-source';

async function run(): Promise<void> {
  await dataSource.initialize();
  try {
    const applied = await dataSource.runMigrations();
    if (applied.length === 0) {
      console.log('No pending migrations.');

      console.log(`Applied ${applied.length} migration(s): ${applied.map((m) => m.name).join(', ')}`);

    await dataSource.destroy();
  }
